ops.title: shipRefuseIndexLock never fires — git add and jj diff hit the lock first
ops.description:
`shipRefuseIndexLock` (`internal/cli/ship_hooks.go:136`) is unreachable end to
end on BOTH lanes. Its tailored refusal — the one carrying the lock's mtime,
which its own doc comment justifies because "git's own failure names neither the
holder nor its age, and only the age separates a live sibling session (seconds)
from a crashed process's leftovers (hours)" — never reaches a user.

**The ordering.** `shipCommit` (`ship.go:471`) runs `shipGitAdd` FIRST on the git
lane. Inside `shipRunHooks` (`ship_hooks.go:54`), `shipHookFiles` runs before the
check at `:69`, and the check is additionally gated behind: a prek config exists,
the changed-file set is non-empty, a jj working copy has git backing, and uvx is
installed.

Observed on a real repository holding `.git/index.lock`:
- git lane dies at `git add -A`:
  `ship: git add: git: exit status 128: fatal: Unable to create
  '<path>/.git/index.lock': File exists.`
- colocated jj lane dies at `jj diff --name-only`:
  `ship: jj diff: jj: exit status 1: Error: Failed to reset Git HEAD state ...
  Could not acquire lock for index file`

**The fake hid it** — the fourth fake-lie found in this effort. `writeShipFakes`'
git answered `"add"*` with `:` (always exit 0) and its jj ignored the lock
entirely, so the check appeared reachable.

**Why the fix is a design call, not mechanical.** Hoisting
`shipRefuseIndexLock(root)` into `shipCommit` ahead of `shipGitAdd` changes WHEN
it fires: it would now fire for repos with no hooks at all, and under
`--no-verify`, neither of which it covers today. And it must NOT fire for
hunk-scoped selections, which commit through a throwaway `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and
never contend for `.git/index.lock`.

Alternatives: accept it as a race-window narrower only and delete the
end-to-end promise from its doc comment (`ship_hooks.go:130`), so it stops
claiming a refusal it cannot deliver.

Not fixed at discovery: a behavior change to when ship refuses, in a file the
discovering lane did not own. `TestShipHooksRefuseHeldIndexLock` now asserts the
property that IS true on a real repository (ship refuses naming the lock, no uvx
spawned, nothing mutated) over a git/jj table, so the tree is green and honest
either way. If the ordering is fixed, that test should go back to asserting
`shipLockRefusal(lock)` verbatim.

ops.text: A held .git/index.lock makes ccx vcs ship refuse with the tailored message naming the lock and its age, on both the git and jj lanes, proven by an end-to-end test
A hunk-scoped ship, which commits through a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE and does not contend for .git/index.lock, is NOT refused
